AcpOnlyUpdate.description: `session/update` bodies only the ACP surface sends.

oneOf.description: The turn ended; the usage rides the prompt result instead.

AcpUpdate.description:
Any `session/update` body: a stream frame or an ACP-only kind. The
`workflows_report` body is the workflow registry's own JSON (untyped here).

AgentCapabilities.description:
Upstream ACP's capability object; hotl's own facts ride under `_meta`, the
spec's place for extensions (0076 D6). No upstream capability is claimed.

ContextKind.description:
What fills the context window, by source (`/context`, plan 0028).

Declaration order IS display order — `Ord` is derived, and both the engine
and the TUI sort by it, so reordering these variants reorders the report.

oneOf.description:
A row this binary does not know. Absorbs a future engine's new kind
without dropping its tokens on the floor — dropping them would
undercount, the one direction this codebase treats as unacceptable.

ContextRow.description:
One row of a `/context` breakdown. `kind` is a stable wire tag, never a
display string — the client owns the label.

EffortAck.description: `effort` is `null` when reset to the provider default.

EgressReply.description: What a client answers `session/request_egress` with. Schema only.

Frame.description:
One `-p --json` frame (and, via `update_frame`, every ACP update body that
mirrors one). Field order is the wire order: under `serde_json`'s
`preserve_order` (on in the default build) a struct serializes in
declaration order, so each variant lists its keys as the old literals did
(0076 D2). Omitted-not-null fields are `Option` + `skip_serializing_if`.

oneOf.description: Streamed answer text.
Streamed reasoning text.
A tool call started; `id` is the provider's `tool_use` id.
A tool call finished; `lines`/`bytes` count the result the model got.
The goal evaluator is judging the turn just finished.
A call waits for a concurrency permit behind `ahead` others.
A fold of `items` history items is starting.
Liveness of a running tool: the tail of its output so far.
The model is writing tool-call input: `calls` calls, `bytes` so far.
A call was denied before it ran.
A call ran without an ask because an allow rule matched.
A protected-class call ran or was refused under bypass, with a notice.
A sub-agent's tool activity; `ok` only on the done phase.
A sub-agent's own words.
One turn's delegation summary.
A cache keep-alive ping was billed.
A request is being retried after `delay_ms`.
The turn moved to a fallback model.
A prompt was queued behind the running turn.
Session spend crossed `pct` of `max_cost_usd`.
A fold finished.
A requested fold had nothing to fold.
The session's model changed; `context_tokens` is the cold-cache rebuild.
The context ladder cleared `count` old tool results.
The todo list changed.
The model presented a plan.
The goal was set (or cleared: `null`).
A memory note was written.
A background job started.
A background job ended.
The session got a generated title (omitted when none was usable).
A `/btw` side question was answered.
A `/btw` side question failed.
The goal evaluator's verdict; `usage` is the goal loop's spend.
The loop ledger's per-turn profile.
The turn ended (`-p --json` only; ACP carries it as the prompt result).
Headless has no human: an ask was denied.
Headless has no human: a question went unanswered.

HotlMeta.description:
hotl speaks its own dialect (`dialect`), shaped after the upstream release
named by `acpSchema`; `extensions` lists every method it speaks.

protocolVersion.description: hotl's own dialect string — not upstream ACP's integer version.

rc.description: The exit status once `done`; `null` while running.

applied.description: `false` = parked until the running turn ends.

oneOf.description: `message` names the knob, for clients that show an outcome's text.

anyOf.description: A typed answer for an ask that wants one.

PermissionReply.description:
What a client answers `session/request_permission` with. Schema only:
`ask_reply_from_result` reads these spellings in this priority (0076 D5).

Phase.description:
The ten boundary events a turn's sample passes through. Declaration order
is the critical-path order the design doc's per-phase deltas price
(`SnapshotReady−BoundaryStart` prices the snapshot transport, etc.) — see
[`DELTA_PAIRS`]. A doom-loop abort or a failed sample can legitimately
skip phases past the point of failure; see [`LoopLedger::stamp`].

`BatchProposed`/`WatermarkDurable` are the one place the critical path
forks: a sample proposes once (the model's own assistant+usage entry) or
twice (that entry, then — only when a tool phase runs — the tool-results
entry). These two phases use [`LoopLedger::restamp`] (last-wins, not
`stamp`'s first-wins), so their recorded position always tracks the
sample's REAL final commit — after `ToolsJoined` when a tool phase ran,
otherwise right after `LastBlockEnd`. Every other phase is written
exactly once by construction, so `stamp`'s first-wins rule is what
applies to them.

**Declaration order is stamp order, not wall order** — and since S2c's
optimistic dispatch those two genuinely diverge. A sample whose request
was dispatched at the *previous* boundary already had bytes on the wire
before this sample's `BoundaryStart`: its true first byte can precede the
previous sample's `WatermarkDurable`, which is the overlap the mechanism
exists for, not a measurement error. Every stamp is taken when the turn
**observes** the event, so the recorded sequence stays monotone and the
summary needs no special case; what a reader must not do is treat
`RequestBuilt→FirstByte` on an adopted sample as a round-trip
measurement. It is the time to *notice* a byte that was already there,
and it is legitimately near zero. ([`width`] saturates either way, so an
out-of-order pair reports `0` rather than wrapping.)

PhaseDeltaSummary.description: One attributable stage's timing across every sample in a flush.

PromptResult.description: The `session/prompt` result, sent when the turn ends.

QuestionOption.description:
One selectable choice in a structured [`Question`] (`ask_user`, tier-1
gap #4). `description` is an optional one-line elaboration shown under
the label.

QuestionReply.description: What a client answers `session/request_question` with. Schema only.

Queued.description: `session/steer` and `session/aside`: `false` = there was no turn to queue on.

ReloadSessionAck.description: `session/reload_config` with an open session (it is re-opened).

protectedWhy.description: Why a protected path is involved, when one is.

RosterEntry.description: `{name, description}` — a skill or workflow in a roster.

SessionOpenResult.description:
The `session/new` / `session/load` / fork result. Absent keys mean
something different from `null` (probe failed / never set / same model).

images.description: Feature detection: an old server never sends it.

Todo.description:
A plan node. Everything past `active_form` is 0056 T1 — all defaulted and
skipped when empty, so a v0.25 `Todos` entry still deserializes and a list
that uses none of it serializes to the same bytes it always did.

acceptance.description: One sentence describing what "done" looks like when no command can say.

active_form.description: Present-tense form shown while in progress ("wiring the gate"); optional.

dependencies.description:
Ids of nodes whose output this one needs. Resolved and cycle-checked
at parse time.

id.description:
`n1..nN`, assigned by `parse_todos` when absent and preserved when the
model sends one back — that stability is what makes `dependencies`
survive a full-state rewrite.

replan.description: The node's own result is expected to change the rest of the plan.

validate_cmd.description:
The exact command that proves this node. Informational to `todo_write`
— nothing refuses a completion; the goal gate (T4) reads it.

TodoStatus.description:
A session checklist item (`todo_write`, M4/tier-1 gap #3). Full-state
replace: the model rewrites the whole list each call, so there is no
separate id/patch shape to reconcile.

`Failed`/`NeedsMoreSteps` (0056 T1) sit **before** the `#[serde(other)]`
arm, so an older binary reads them as `Unknown` — which every renderer
already tolerates — rather than failing the whole entry.

oneOf.description: Tried and did not work. Distinct from `Pending`: it has been attempted.
The step turned out to be bigger than one step — it needs splitting.

TokenUsage.description: Normalized usage; fields absent from a provider response default to zero.

cache_creation_1h_input_tokens.description:
Cache-write tokens billed at the 1-hour TTL rate (2x input, vs. 1.25x
for the 5-minute default). See `cache_creation_5m_input_tokens`.

cache_creation_5m_input_tokens.description:
Cache-write tokens billed at the 5-minute TTL rate — a refinement of
`cache_creation_input_tokens` (which stays the authoritative total),
not a replacement for it. `skip_serializing_if` keeps a payload with
no per-TTL breakdown byte-identical to one from before this field
existed: this struct is persisted in the session log and serialized
into `--json`/ACP frames, so a zero bucket must stay invisible on
the wire.

UsageFrame.description:
`TokenUsage` plus the derived `hit_ratio` and `cost_usd`, each omitted
when there is nothing to report.

cache_creation_1h_input_tokens.description:
Cache-write tokens billed at the 1-hour TTL rate (2x input, vs. 1.25x
for the 5-minute default). See `cache_creation_5m_input_tokens`.

cache_creation_5m_input_tokens.description:

`cache_creation_input_tokens` (which stays the authoritative total),
not a replacement for it. `skip_serializing_if` keeps a payload with
no per-TTL breakdown byte-identical to one from before this field
existed: this struct is persisted in the session log and serialized
